title: Bind first selected gauge44 provider and rule out fixed QQ16 role conjugacy
body:
The first selected gauge44 provider is not corrected QQ16 F0 under a fixed invertible change of persistent roles. This package binds the literal selected `calls[0]` (replica 0, stage 0, time 0), its embedded program hash, all 704 owner IDs and source frame arrays, then replays both actual words on 712 independent formal inputs at the constant-character/common-cover specialization.

Selected gauge44 gives `G(x,y)=(x,y+x)`. Corrected QQ16 first differs at `X_0=(x_76-x_81+x_87+x_92)/2`. Persistent traces 704 versus 600 exclude every fixed invertible role conjugacy, including mixing all 480 helpers. Exact rational elimination gives `rank(Q-G)=24`; since Q is invertible, any post-adapter E satisfying EQ=G has `rank(E-I)=24`. The complete literal scalar invoice is 198766 versus 211210 (+12444), before any repair. Both words return all 480 arbitrary helpers and clear eight owned private outputs.

The mapping class and limits are explicit: different entrance/exit encodings and paid adapters remain open. The package stops at the F0 mismatch and does not assume a matched B1 decoder cut. It supplies no physical adapter, complete supplier, selected-frontier update, or unrestricted impossibility theorem. The native difference of removing eight H8 centres and adding eight H1 lines is conditional on a valid replacement.

Validation: registered package PASS; optimized warning-strict replay; all 712 symbolic inputs; independent R/K formula check; source and QQ16 coefficient mutation rejection; normal/optimized Git-free read-only export; source-hash and typed-receipt rejection; receipt overwrite refusal. Root independently reviewed the proof/code and reran optimized controls. All source bytes are pinned before parsing and no predecessor executable is imported.

Builds on the retained selected archive, corrected joint-query construction and bridge/scalar reviews; extends #3976's missing-binding audit with the actual provider calculation. Distinct from the decoder work in #4003/#4015 and tekuuu's fixed 104-owner/common-frame consumer obstruction in #4030. Original source contributors retain credit. New work by Chris R / Clear1nsight with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent human review claimed.
